name: cadastral-digitizer
description: Browser extension for digitizing cadastral and GIS parcels from map portals, scanned sheets, images and PDF pages. This package.json exists only to run the test suite; the extension itself ships as plain unbundled files with no runtime dependencies.
author: Md Salim Ansari
//: Both dev dependencies are OPTIONAL. With neither installed, `npm test` still
runs 477 tests and the 72 that need a browser skip cleanly — which is what
makes the suite useful to someone who has just unzipped the extension.
npm install --no-save jsdom            enables 58 DOM integration tests
npm install --no-save playwright-core  enables 14 real-Chrome E2E tests
playwright-core also needs a Chrome binary on the machine; the E2E file looks
for the usual locations and skips if it finds none.
--test-force-exit was removed in 16.3.0. It was added to stop the runner
hanging on jsdom timers and Playwright contexts, but once those were being
closed properly it was no longer needed -- and it was TRUNCATING the TAP
output, so consecutive runs reported 414, 416 and 418 tests from an unchanged
suite. A run that can silently drop results can silently drop a failure, which
defeats the point of having the suite.
